Calcination is the process of heating a concentrated ore strongly below its melting point in the absence or limited supply of air to remove volatile impurities, moisture, or carbon dioxide, converting carbonates and hydrated oxides into metal oxides.

Step 2: Evaluation of Reactions
- \(\mathrm{CaCO}_3 \longrightarrow \mathrm{CaO} + \mathrm{CO}_2\) is thermal decomposition of a carbonate in the absence of air, which is calcination.
- \(\mathrm{Al}_2\mathrm{O}_3 \cdot x\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O} \longrightarrow \mathrm{Al}_2\mathrm{O}_3 + x\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\) is removal of water of hydration by heating, which is calcination.
- The reactions involving \(\mathrm{O}_2\) with sulphide ores (\(\mathrm{FeS}_2\) and \(\mathrm{ZnS}\)) to form oxides and \(\mathrm{SO}_2\) are examples of roasting, not calcination.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Therefore, \(\mathrm{CaCO}_3 \longrightarrow \mathrm{CaO} + \mathrm{CO}_2\) and \(\mathrm{Al}_2\mathrm{O}_3 \cdot x\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O} \longrightarrow \mathrm{Al}_2\mathrm{O}_3 + x\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\) occur during calcination.

चरण 1: अवधारणात्मक सिद्धांत
निस्तापन वह प्रक्रम है जिसमें सांद्रित अयस्क को वायु की अनुपस्थिति या सीमित आपूर्ति में उसके गलनांक से कम ताप पर प्रबलता से गर्म किया जाता है ताकि वाष्पशील अशुद्धियाँ, नमी या कार्बन डाइऑक्साइड दूर हो जाएँ और कार्बोनेट तथा जलयोजित ऑक्साइड धातु ऑक्साइडों में परिवर्तित हो जाएँ।

चरण 2: अभिक्रियाओं का मूल्यांकन
- \(\mathrm{CaCO}_3 \longrightarrow \mathrm{CaO} + \mathrm{CO}_2\) वायु की अनुपस्थिति में कार्बोनेट का तापीय अपघटन है, जो निस्तापन है।
- \(\mathrm{Al}_2\mathrm{O}_3 \cdot x\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O} \longrightarrow \mathrm{Al}_2\mathrm{O}_3 + x\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\) गर्म करके क्रिस्टलन जल को हटाना है, जो निस्तापन है।
- सल्फाइड अयस्कों (\(\mathrm{FeS}_2\) और \(\mathrm{ZnS}\)) की \(\mathrm{O}_2\) के साथ ऑक्साइड और \(\mathrm{SO}_2\) बनाने वाली अभिक्रियाएँ भर्जन के उदाहरण हैं, निस्तापन के नहीं।

चरण 3: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
अतः, \(\mathrm{CaCO}_3 \longrightarrow \mathrm{CaO} + \mathrm{CO}_2\) और \(\mathrm{Al}_2\mathrm{O}_3 \cdot x\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O} \longrightarrow \mathrm{Al}_2\mathrm{O}_3 + x\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\) निस्तापन के दौरान होती हैं।

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQII_Q22 - Ores whose calcined ore is reduced by carbon

questiontext.text:
For the metallurgical process of which of the ores calcined ore can be reduced by carbon?

निम्नलिखित में से किन अयस्कों के धातुकर्म प्रक्रम के लिए निस्तापित अयस्क को कार्बन द्वारा अपचयित किया जा सकता है?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Calcination is applied to oxide, hydroxide, and carbonate ores (not sulphide ores, which undergo roasting). After calcination, the resulting metal oxide is reduced by carbon (coke) in a smelting step if thermodynamically feasible.

Step 2: Evaluation of Ores
- Haematite (\(\mathrm{Fe}_2\mathrm{O}_3\)) is an oxide ore; after calcination (heating to remove moisture), it is reduced by carbon/CO in a blast furnace.
- Calamine (\(\mathrm{ZnCO}_3\)) is a carbonate ore; it is calcined to \(\mathrm{ZnO}\), which is then reduced by carbon (coke) at high temperature.
- Iron pyrites (\(\mathrm{FeS}_2\)) and sphalerite (\(\mathrm{ZnS}\)) are sulphide ores; they are subjected to roasting, not calcination.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Therefore, for haematite and calamine, the calcined ore can be reduced by carbon.

चरण 1: अवधारणात्मक सिद्धांत
निस्तापन ऑक्साइड, हाइड्रॉक्साइड और कार्बोनेट अयस्कों पर लागू होता है (सल्फाइड अयस्कों पर नहीं, जिनका भर्जन किया जाता है)। निस्तापन के बाद, यदि ऊष्मागतिक रूप से संभव हो, तो प्राप्त धातु ऑक्साइड को प्रगलन पद में कार्बन (कोक) द्वारा अपचयित किया जाता है।

चरण 2: अयस्कों का मूल्यांकन
- हेमेटाइट (\(\mathrm{Fe}_2\mathrm{O}_3\)) एक ऑक्साइड अयस्क है; निस्तापन (नमी हटाने के लिए गर्म करना) के बाद, इसे वात्या भट्ठी में कार्बन/CO द्वारा अपचयित किया जाता है।
- कैलेमाइन (\(\mathrm{ZnCO}_3\)) एक कार्बोनेट अयस्क है; इसे \(\mathrm{ZnO}\) में निस्तापित किया जाता है, जिसे फिर उच्च ताप पर कार्बन (कोक) द्वारा अपचयित किया जाता है।
- आयरन पाइराइट (\(\mathrm{FeS}_2\)) और स्फैलेराइट (\(\mathrm{ZnS}\)) सल्फाइड अयस्क हैं; इनका निस्तापन नहीं बल्कि भर्जन किया जाता है।

चरण 3: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
अतः, हेमेटाइट और कैलेमाइन के लिए निस्तापित अयस्क को कार्बन द्वारा अपचयित किया जा सकता है।

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQII_Q23 - Main reactions in blast furnace for iron extraction

questiontext.text:
The main reactions occurring in blast furnace during extraction of iron from haematite are

हेमेटाइट से आयरन के निष्कर्षण के दौरान वात्या भट्ठी में होने वाली मुख्य अभिक्रियाएँ हैं

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
In the blast furnace, haematite (\(\mathrm{Fe}_2\mathrm{O}_3\)) is reduced to iron by carbon monoxide (\(\mathrm{CO}\)), while limestone (\(\mathrm{CaCO}_3\)) decomposes to \(\mathrm{CaO}\), which acts as a basic flux to remove acidic silica (\(\mathrm{SiO}_2\)) gangue as slag.

Step 2: Evaluation of Reactions
- \(\mathrm{Fe}_2\mathrm{O}_3 + 3\mathrm{CO} \longrightarrow 2\mathrm{Fe} + 3\mathrm{CO}_2\) is a main reduction reaction in the blast furnace.
- \(\mathrm{CaO} + \mathrm{SiO}_2 \longrightarrow \mathrm{CaSiO}_3\) is the main slag-formation reaction in the blast furnace.
- \(\mathrm{FeO} + \mathrm{SiO}_2 \longrightarrow \mathrm{FeSiO}_3\) occurs during copper extraction in a reverberatory furnace, not in the iron blast furnace.
- Direct reduction of \(\mathrm{Fe}_2\mathrm{O}_3\) by solid carbon (\(\mathrm{Fe}_2\mathrm{O}_3 + 3\mathrm{C} \longrightarrow 2\mathrm{Fe} + 3\mathrm{CO}\)) is not a primary reaction in the blast furnace; \(\mathrm{Fe}_2\mathrm{O}_3\) is reduced mainly by \(\mathrm{CO}\).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Thus, the main reactions occurring in the blast furnace are \(\mathrm{Fe}_2\mathrm{O}_3 + 3\mathrm{CO} \longrightarrow 2\mathrm{Fe} + 3\mathrm{CO}_2\) and \(\mathrm{CaO} + \mathrm{SiO}_2 \longrightarrow \mathrm{CaSiO}_3\).

चरण 1: अवधारणात्मक सिद्धांत
वात्या भट्ठी में, हेमेटाइट (\(\mathrm{Fe}_2\mathrm{O}_3\)) को कार्बन मोनोऑक्साइड (\(\mathrm{CO}\)) द्वारा आयरन में अपचयित किया जाता है, जबकि चूना पत्थर (\(\mathrm{CaCO}_3\)) अपघटित होकर \(\mathrm{CaO}\) बनाता है, जो अम्लीय सिलिका (\(\mathrm{SiO}_2\)) आधात्री को धातुमल के रूप में हटाने के लिए क्षारीय गालक के रूप में कार्य करता है।

चरण 2: अभिक्रियाओं का मूल्यांकन
- \(\mathrm{Fe}_2\mathrm{O}_3 + 3\mathrm{CO} \longrightarrow 2\mathrm{Fe} + 3\mathrm{CO}_2\) वात्या भट्ठी में एक मुख्य अपचयन अभिक्रिया है।
- \(\mathrm{CaO} + \mathrm{SiO}_2 \longrightarrow \mathrm{CaSiO}_3\) वात्या भट्ठी में मुख्य धातुमल-निर्माण अभिक्रिया है।
- \(\mathrm{FeO} + \mathrm{SiO}_2 \longrightarrow \mathrm{FeSiO}_3\) परावर्तनी भट्ठी में कॉपर निष्कर्षण के दौरान होती है, आयरन की वात्या भट्ठी में नहीं।
- ठोस कार्बन द्वारा \(\mathrm{Fe}_2\mathrm{O}_3\) का प्रत्यक्ष अपचयन (\(\mathrm{Fe}_2\mathrm{O}_3 + 3\mathrm{C} \longrightarrow 2\mathrm{Fe} + 3\mathrm{CO}\)) वात्या भट्ठी में प्राथमिक अभिक्रिया नहीं है; \(\mathrm{Fe}_2\mathrm{O}_3\) मुख्यतः \(\mathrm{CO}\) द्वारा अपचयित होता है।

चरण 3: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
अतः, वात्या भट्ठी में होने वाली मुख्य अभिक्रियाएँ \(\mathrm{Fe}_2\mathrm{O}_3 + 3\mathrm{CO} \longrightarrow 2\mathrm{Fe} + 3\mathrm{CO}_2\) और \(\mathrm{CaO} + \mathrm{SiO}_2 \longrightarrow \mathrm{CaSiO}_3\) हैं।

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQII_Q24 - Vapour phase refining methods

questiontext.text:
In which of the following method of purification, metal is converted to its volatile compound which is decomposed to give pure metal?

निम्नलिखित में से किस शुद्धिकरण विधि में, धातु को उसके वाष्पशील यौगिक में परिवर्तित किया जाता है जिसे शुद्ध धातु देने के लिए अपघटित किया जाता है?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Vapour phase refining involves converting an impure metal into a volatile compound, which is then collected and decomposed at a higher temperature to yield the pure metal.

Step 2: Evaluation of Purification Methods
- Heating with a stream of carbon monoxide corresponds to the Mond process for nickel, where \(\mathrm{Ni}\) forms volatile \(\mathrm{Ni(CO)}_4\), which decomposes on further heating to give pure \(\mathrm{Ni}\).
- Heating with iodine corresponds to the van Arkel method for \(\mathrm{Zr}\) and \(\mathrm{Ti}\), which form volatile tetraiodides (\(\mathrm{ZrI}_4\), \(\mathrm{TiI}_4\)) that decompose on a hot tungsten filament to give pure metal.
- Liquation and distillation are physical separation methods based on differences in melting points and boiling points respectively, without forming a volatile chemical compound.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Therefore, heating with a stream of carbon monoxide and heating with iodine involve conversion of the metal into a volatile compound followed by decomposition.

चरण 1: अवधारणात्मक सिद्धांत
वाष्प प्रावस्था परिष्करण में अशुद्ध धातु को एक वाष्पशील यौगिक में परिवर्तित किया जाता है, जिसे एकत्र करके उच्च ताप पर अपघटित करने पर शुद्ध धातु प्राप्त होती है।

चरण 2: शुद्धिकरण विधियों का मूल्यांकन
- कार्बन मोनोऑक्साइड की धारा के साथ गर्म करना निकेल के लिए मॉन्ड प्रक्रम से संबंधित है, जहाँ \(\mathrm{Ni}\) वाष्पशील \(\mathrm{Ni(CO)}_4\) बनाता है, जो आगे गर्म करने पर अपघटित होकर शुद्ध \(\mathrm{Ni}\) देता है।
- आयोडीन के साथ गर्म करना \(\mathrm{Zr}\) और \(\mathrm{Ti}\) के लिए वान आरकेल विधि से संबंधित है, जो वाष्पशील टेट्राआयोडाइड (\(\mathrm{ZrI}_4\), \(\mathrm{TiI}_4\)) बनाते हैं जो गर्म टंगस्टन तंतु पर अपघटित होकर शुद्ध धातु देते हैं।
- द्रवण और आसवन क्रमशः गलनांक और क्वथनांक के अंतर पर आधारित भौतिक पृथक्करण विधियाँ हैं, जिनमें कोई वाष्पशील रासायनिक यौगिक नहीं बनता है।

चरण 3: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
अतः, कार्बन मोनोऑक्साइड की धारा के साथ गर्म करना तथा आयोडीन के साथ गर्म करना धातु को वाष्पशील यौगिक में परिवर्तित करके अपघटित करने से संबंधित हैं।

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQII_Q25 - Correct statements on depressant and blister copper

questiontext.text:
Which of the following statements are correct?

निम्नलिखित में से कौन-से कथन सही हैं?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
This question tests concepts of froth flotation depressants, copper matte composition, blister copper formation, and zinc extraction.

Step 2: Evaluation of Statements
1. In froth flotation, a depressant (such as \(\mathrm{NaCN}\)) selectively prevents a certain type of mineral particle (such as \(\mathrm{ZnS}\)) from coming to the froth. This statement is correct.
2. Copper matte contains \(\mathrm{Cu}_2\mathrm{S}\) and \(\mathrm{FeS}\), not \(\mathrm{ZnS}\). This statement is incorrect.
3. Solidified copper obtained after autoreduction has a blistered appearance due to the evolution of \(\mathrm{SO}_2\) gas during solidification (blister copper). This statement is correct.
4. Zinc is extracted by reduction of \(\mathrm{ZnO}\) with carbon (coke), not by self-reduction. This statement is incorrect.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Therefore, the statements regarding the role of a depressant and the blistered appearance of solidified copper due to evolution of \(\mathrm{SO}_2\) are correct.

चरण 1: अवधारणात्मक सिद्धांत
यह प्रश्न फेन प्लवन अवनमक, कॉपर मैट के संघटन, फफोलेदार कॉपर के निर्माण और ज़िंक के निष्कर्षण की अवधारणाओं की जाँच करता है।

चरण 2: कथनों का मूल्यांकन
1. फेन प्लवन में, एक अवनमक (जैसे \(\mathrm{NaCN}\)) चयनात्मक रूप से एक निश्चित प्रकार के खनिज कण (जैसे \(\mathrm{ZnS}\)) को फेन में आने से रोकता है। यह कथन सही है।
2. कॉपर मैट में \(\mathrm{Cu}_2\mathrm{S}\) और \(\mathrm{FeS}\) होता है, \(\mathrm{ZnS}\) नहीं। यह कथन गलत है।
3. स्वतः अपचयन के बाद प्राप्त ठोस कॉपर की सतह जमने के दौरान \(\mathrm{SO}_2\) गैस के निकलने के कारण फफोलेदार दिखती है (फफोलेदार कॉपर)। यह कथन सही है।
4. ज़िंक का निष्कर्षण कार्बन (कोक) के साथ \(\mathrm{ZnO}\) के अपचयन द्वारा किया जाता है, स्व-अपचयन द्वारा नहीं। यह कथन गलत है।

चरण 3: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
अतः, अवनमक की भूमिका तथा \(\mathrm{SO}_2\) के निकलने के कारण ठोस कॉपर के फफोलेदार दिखाई देने से संबंधित कथन सही हैं।

answer.text: A depressant prevents certain type of particle to come to the froth.
The solidified copper obtained from reverberatory furnace has blistered appearance due to evolution of \(\mathrm{SO}_2\) during the extraction.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQII_Q26 - Thermodynamics of chlorine extraction from brine

questiontext.text:
In the extraction of chlorine from brine

ब्राइन से क्लोरीन के निष्कर्षण में

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The extraction of chlorine from brine is carried out by electrolysis, as the overall chemical reaction \(2\mathrm{Cl}^-(aq) + 2\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}(l) \longrightarrow 2\mathrm{OH}^-(aq) + \mathrm{H}_2(g) + \mathrm{Cl}_2(g)\) is non-spontaneous.

Step 2: Thermodynamic Evaluation
For this overall reaction, \(\Delta G^{\ominus} = +422\,\mathrm{kJ}\), which is positive. Using the relation \(\Delta G^{\ominus} = -nFE^{\ominus}\), a positive \(\Delta G^{\ominus}\) corresponds to a negative \(E^{\ominus}\) value (\(E^{\ominus} = -2.2\,\mathrm{V}\)). Hence, an external emf greater than \(2.2\,\mathrm{V}\) is required to drive the electrolysis.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Therefore, \(\Delta G^{\ominus}\) for the overall reaction is positive, and \(E^{\ominus}\) for the overall reaction has a negative value.

चरण 1: अवधारणात्मक सिद्धांत
ब्राइन से क्लोरीन का निष्कर्षण वैद्युत अपघटन द्वारा किया जाता है, क्योंकि समग्र रासायनिक अभिक्रिया \(2\mathrm{Cl}^-(aq) + 2\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}(l) \longrightarrow 2\mathrm{OH}^-(aq) + \mathrm{H}_2(g) + \mathrm{Cl}_2(g)\) अस्वतः प्रवर्तित होती है।

चरण 2: ऊष्मागतिकीय मूल्यांकन
इस समग्र अभिक्रिया के लिए, \(\Delta G^{\ominus} = +422\,\mathrm{kJ}\) है, जो धनात्मक है। संबंध \(\Delta G^{\ominus} = -nFE^{\ominus}\) का उपयोग करने पर, धनात्मक \(\Delta G^{\ominus}\) एक ऋणात्मक \(E^{\ominus}\) मान (\(E^{\ominus} = -2.2\,\mathrm{V}\)) के संगत होता है। अतः, वैद्युत अपघटन को चलाने के लिए \(2.2\,\mathrm{V}\) से अधिक बाहरी विद्युत वाहक बल की आवश्यकता होती है।

चरण 3: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
अतः, समग्र अभिक्रिया के लिए \(\Delta G^{\ominus}\) धनात्मक है और समग्र अभिक्रिया के लिए \(E^{\ominus}\) का मान ऋणात्मक है।

answer.text: \(\Delta G^{\ominus}\) for the overall reaction is negative.
\(\Delta G^{\ominus}\) for the overall reaction is positive.
\(E^{\ominus}\) for overall reaction has negative value.
\(E^{\ominus}\) for overall reaction has positive value.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MATCHING_Q45 - Match alloys and ores with their compositions

questiontext.text:
Match the items of Column I with items of Column II and assign the correct code:

Column IColumn II
(A) Pendulum(1) Chrome steel
(B) Malachite(2) Nickel steel
(C) Calamine(3) \(\mathrm{Na}_{3} \mathrm{AlF}_{6}\)
(D) Cryolite(4) \(\mathrm{CuCO}_{3} \cdot \mathrm{Cu(OH)}_{2}\)
(5) \(\mathrm{ZnCO}_{3}\)

स्तंभ I की मदों को स्तंभ II की मदों से सुमेलित कीजिए और सही कूट का चयन कीजिए:

स्तंभ Iस्तंभ II
(A) लोलक (पेंडुलम)(1) क्रोम स्टील
(B) मैलेकाइट(2) निकेल स्टील
(C) कैलेमाइन(3) \(\mathrm{Na}_{3} \mathrm{AlF}_{6}\)
(D) क्रायोलाइट(4) \(\mathrm{CuCO}_{3} \cdot \mathrm{Cu(OH)}_{2}\)
(5) \(\mathrm{ZnCO}_{3}\)

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Each item in Column I corresponds to a specific alloy or mineral formula in Column II.

Step 2: Item-by-Item Matching
- Pendulum: Nickel steel (such as Invar, containing about \(36\%\,\mathrm{Ni}\)) has a negligible coefficient of thermal expansion and is used in making pendulums. Thus, \(\mathrm{A} \rightarrow (2)\).
- Malachite: It is a basic copper carbonate ore with the formula \(\mathrm{CuCO}_3 \cdot \mathrm{Cu(OH)}_2\). Thus, \(\mathrm{B} \rightarrow (4)\).
- Calamine: It is a carbonate ore of zinc with the formula \(\mathrm{ZnCO}_3\). Thus, \(\mathrm{C} \rightarrow (5)\).
- Cryolite: It is a fluoride mineral of aluminium with the formula \(\mathrm{Na}_3\mathrm{AlF}_6\). Thus, \(\mathrm{D} \rightarrow (3)\).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Therefore, the correct matching code is \(\mathrm{A\ (2)\ B\ (4)\ C\ (5)\ D\ (3)}\).

चरण 1: अवधारणात्मक सिद्धांत
स्तंभ I की प्रत्येक मद स्तंभ II में दिए गए एक विशिष्ट मिश्रधातु या खनिज सूत्र से संबंधित है।

चरण 2: प्रत्येक मद का सुमेलन
- लोलक (पेंडुलम): निकेल स्टील (जैसे इनवार, जिसमें लगभग \(36\%\,\mathrm{Ni}\) होता है) का तापीय प्रसार गुणांक नगण्य होता है और इसका उपयोग लोलक बनाने में किया जाता है। अतः, \(\mathrm{A} \rightarrow (2)\)।
- मैलेकाइट: यह कॉपर का एक क्षारीय कार्बोनेट अयस्क है जिसका सूत्र \(\mathrm{CuCO}_3 \cdot \mathrm{Cu(OH)}_2\) है। अतः, \(\mathrm{B} \rightarrow (4)\)।
- कैलेमाइन: यह ज़िंक का एक कार्बोनेट अयस्क है जिसका सूत्र \(\mathrm{ZnCO}_3\) है। अतः, \(\mathrm{C} \rightarrow (5)\)।
- क्रायोलाइट: यह ऐलुमिनियम का एक फ्लोराइड खनिज है जिसका सूत्र \(\mathrm{Na}_3\mathrm{AlF}_6\) है। अतः, \(\mathrm{D} \rightarrow (3)\)।

चरण 3: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
अतः, सही सुमेलन कूट \(\mathrm{A\ (2)\ B\ (4)\ C\ (5)\ D\ (3)}\) है।

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MATCHING_Q46 - Match purification techniques with principles and metals

questiontext.text:
Match the items of Column I with the items of Column II and assign the correct code:

Column IColumn II
(A) Coloured bands(1) Zone refining
(B) Impure metal to volatile complex(2) Fractional distillation
(C) Purification of Ge and Si(3) Mond Process
(D) Purification of mercury(4) Chromatography
(5) Liquation

स्तंभ I की मदों को स्तंभ II की मदों से सुमेलित कीजिए और सही कूट का चयन कीजिए:

स्तंभ Iस्तंभ II
(A) रंगीन पट्टियाँ (बैंड)(1) ज़ोन परिष्करण
(B) अशुद्ध धातु से वाष्पशील संकुल(2) प्रभाजी आसवन
(C) Ge और Si का शुद्धिकरण(3) मॉन्ड प्रक्रम
(D) मरकरी का शुद्धिकरण(4) वर्णलेखिकी (क्रोमैटोग्राफी)
(5) द्रवण

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Each characteristic or metal purification requirement in Column I corresponds to a specific refining technique in Column II.

Step 2: Item-by-Item Matching
- Coloured bands: Chromatography separates components of a mixture based on differential adsorption on an adsorbent column, often appearing as distinct coloured bands. Thus, \(\mathrm{A} \rightarrow (4)\).
- Impure metal to volatile complex: In the Mond Process, impure nickel is converted into volatile nickel tetracarbonyl, \(\mathrm{Ni(CO)}_4\), which is then decomposed to give pure nickel. Thus, \(\mathrm{B} \rightarrow (3)\).
- Purification of \(\mathrm{Ge}\) and \(\mathrm{Si}\): Semiconductors like \(\mathrm{Ge}\) and \(\mathrm{Si}\) are purified to ultrapure grade by zone refining. Thus, \(\mathrm{C} \rightarrow (1)\).
- Purification of mercury: Low-boiling metals such as mercury (\(\mathrm{Hg}\)) and zinc (\(\mathrm{Zn}\)) are purified by fractional distillation (distillation). Thus, \(\mathrm{D} \rightarrow (2)\).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Therefore, the correct matching code is \(\mathrm{A\ (4)\ B\ (3)\ C\ (1)\ D\ (2)}\).

चरण 1: अवधारणात्मक सिद्धांत
स्तंभ I की प्रत्येक विशेषता या धातु शुद्धिकरण आवश्यकता स्तंभ II में एक विशिष्ट परिष्करण तकनीक से संबंधित है।

चरण 2: प्रत्येक मद का सुमेलन
- रंगीन पट्टियाँ (बैंड): वर्णलेखिकी (क्रोमैटोग्राफी) अधिशोषक स्तंभ पर विभेदक अधिशोषण के आधार पर मिश्रण के घटकों को पृथक करती है, जो प्रायः स्पष्ट रंगीन पट्टियों के रूप में दिखाई देते हैं। अतः, \(\mathrm{A} \rightarrow (4)\)।
- अशुद्ध धातु से वाष्पशील संकुल: मॉन्ड प्रक्रम में, अशुद्ध निकेल को वाष्पशील निकेल टेट्राकार्बोनिल, \(\mathrm{Ni(CO)}_4\) में परिवर्तित किया जाता है, जिसे फिर शुद्ध निकेल प्राप्त करने के लिए अपघटित किया जाता है। अतः, \(\mathrm{B} \rightarrow (3)\)।
- \(\mathrm{Ge}\) और \(\mathrm{Si}\) का शुद्धिकरण: \(\mathrm{Ge}\) और \(\mathrm{Si}\) जैसे अर्धचालकों को ज़ोन परिष्करण द्वारा अतिशुद्ध स्तर तक शुद्ध किया जाता है। अतः, \(\mathrm{C} \rightarrow (1)\)।
- मरकरी का शुद्धिकरण: मरकरी (\(\mathrm{Hg}\)) और ज़िंक (\(\mathrm{Zn}\)) जैसी कम क्वथनांक वाली धातुओं का शुद्धिकरण प्रभाजी आसवन (आसवन) द्वारा किया जाता है। अतः, \(\mathrm{D} \rightarrow (2)\)।

चरण 3: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
अतः, सही सुमेलन कूट \(\mathrm{A\ (4)\ B\ (3)\ C\ (1)\ D\ (2)}\) है।

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MATCHING_Q47 - Match metallurgical processes with their applications

questiontext.text:
Match items of Column I with the items of Column II and assign the correct code:

Column IColumn II
(A) Cyanide process(1) Ultrapure Ge
(B) Froth Floatation Process(2) Dressing of ZnS
(C) Electrolytic reduction(3) Extraction of Al
(D) Zone refining(4) Extraction of Au
(5) Purification of Ni

स्तंभ I की मदों को स्तंभ II की मदों से सुमेलित कीजिए और सही कूट का चयन कीजिए:

स्तंभ Iस्तंभ II
(A) सायनाइड प्रक्रम(1) अतिशुद्ध Ge
(B) फेन प्लवन प्रक्रम(2) ZnS का सांद्रण
(C) वैद्युत अपघटनी अपचयन(3) Al का निष्कर्षण
(D) ज़ोन परिष्करण(4) Au का निष्कर्षण
(5) Ni का शुद्धिकरण

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Each metallurgical process in Column I has a specific metal extraction or purification application listed in Column II.

Step 2: Item-by-Item Matching
- Cyanide process: Used for the extraction of gold (\(\mathrm{Au}\)) and silver (\(\mathrm{Ag}\)) by leaching with \(\mathrm{CN}^-\). Thus, \(\mathrm{A} \rightarrow (4)\).
- Froth Floatation Process: Used for concentration (dressing) of sulphide ores such as \(\mathrm{ZnS}\). Thus, \(\mathrm{B} \rightarrow (2)\).
- Electrolytic reduction: Used for the extraction of reactive metals such as aluminium (\(\mathrm{Al}\)) from molten alumina (Hall-Heroult process). Thus, \(\mathrm{C} \rightarrow (3)\).
- Zone refining: Used for obtaining ultrapure semiconductors such as germanium (\(\mathrm{Ge}\)). Thus, \(\mathrm{D} \rightarrow (1)\).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Therefore, the correct matching code is \(\mathrm{A\ (4)\ B\ (2)\ C\ (3)\ D\ (1)}\).

चरण 1: अवधारणात्मक सिद्धांत
स्तंभ I में दिए गए प्रत्येक धातुकर्म प्रक्रम का एक विशिष्ट धातु निष्कर्षण या शुद्धिकरण अनुप्रयोग स्तंभ II में सूचीबद्ध है।

चरण 2: प्रत्येक मद का सुमेलन
- सायनाइड प्रक्रम: \(\mathrm{CN}^-\) के साथ निक्षालन द्वारा गोल्ड (\(\mathrm{Au}\)) और सिल्वर (\(\mathrm{Ag}\)) के निष्कर्षण के लिए उपयोग किया जाता है। अतः, \(\mathrm{A} \rightarrow (4)\)।
- फेन प्लवन प्रक्रम: \(\mathrm{ZnS}\) जैसे सल्फाइड अयस्कों के सांद्रण के लिए उपयोग किया जाता है। अतः, \(\mathrm{B} \rightarrow (2)\)।
- वैद्युत अपघटनी अपचयन: गलित ऐलुमिना से ऐलुमिनियम (\(\mathrm{Al}\)) जैसी सक्रिय धातुओं के निष्कर्षण के लिए उपयोग किया जाता है (हॉल-हेरॉल्ट प्रक्रम)। अतः, \(\mathrm{C} \rightarrow (3)\)।
- ज़ोन परिष्करण: जर्मेनियम (\(\mathrm{Ge}\)) जैसे अतिशुद्ध अर्धचालक प्राप्त करने के लिए उपयोग किया जाता है। अतः, \(\mathrm{D} \rightarrow (1)\)।

चरण 3: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
अतः, सही सुमेलन कूट \(\mathrm{A\ (4)\ B\ (2)\ C\ (3)\ D\ (1)}\) है।

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MATCHING_Q48 - Match minerals and reagents with their chemical identities

questiontext.text:
Match the items of Column I with the items of Column II and assign the correct code:

Column IColumn II
(A) Sapphire(1) \(\mathrm{Al}_{2} \mathrm{O}_{3}\)
(B) Sphalerite(2) NaCN
(C) Depressant(3) Co
(D) Corundum(4) ZnS
(5) \(\mathrm{Fe}_2\mathrm{O}_3\)

स्तंभ I की मदों को स्तंभ II की मदों से सुमेलित कीजिए और सही कूट का चयन कीजिए:

स्तंभ Iस्तंभ II
(A) नीलम (सैफायर)(1) \(\mathrm{Al}_{2} \mathrm{O}_{3}\)
(B) स्फैलेराइट(2) NaCN
(C) अवनमक(3) Co
(D) कोरंडम(4) ZnS
(5) \(\mathrm{Fe}_2\mathrm{O}_3\)

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Each mineral, gemstone, or metallurgical reagent in Column I corresponds to its chemical constituent or formula in Column II.

Step 2: Item-by-Item Matching
- Sapphire: A gemstone variety of corundum containing traces of cobalt (\(\mathrm{Co}\)) (which imparts its blue colour). Thus, \(\mathrm{A} \rightarrow (3)\).
- Sphalerite: It is the principal sulphide ore of zinc, chemically \(\mathrm{ZnS}\). Thus, \(\mathrm{B} \rightarrow (4)\).
- Depressant: Sodium cyanide (\(\mathrm{NaCN}\)) is used as a depressant in froth flotation to separate \(\mathrm{ZnS}\) from \(\mathrm{PbS}\). Thus, \(\mathrm{C} \rightarrow (2)\).
- Corundum: It is a crystalline mineral form of aluminium oxide, \(\mathrm{Al}_2\mathrm{O}_3\). Thus, \(\mathrm{D} \rightarrow (1)\).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Therefore, the correct matching code is \(\mathrm{A\ (3)\ B\ (4)\ C\ (2)\ D\ (1)}\).

चरण 1: अवधारणात्मक सिद्धांत
स्तंभ I में प्रत्येक खनिज, रत्न या धातुकर्म अभिकर्मक स्तंभ II में उसके रासायनिक घटक या सूत्र से संबंधित है।

चरण 2: प्रत्येक मद का सुमेलन
- नीलम (सैफायर): कोरंडम की एक रत्न किस्म है जिसमें कोबाल्ट (\(\mathrm{Co}\)) के अंश होते हैं। अतः, \(\mathrm{A} \rightarrow (3)\)।
- स्फैलेराइट: यह ज़िंक का मुख्य सल्फाइड अयस्क है, जो रासायनिक रूप से \(\mathrm{ZnS}\) है। अतः, \(\mathrm{B} \rightarrow (4)\)।
- अवनमक: फेन प्लवन में \(\mathrm{PbS}\) से \(\mathrm{ZnS}\) को पृथक करने के लिए सोडियम सायनाइड (\(\mathrm{NaCN}\)) का उपयोग अवनमक के रूप में किया जाता है। अतः, \(\mathrm{C} \rightarrow (2)\)।
- कोरंडम: यह ऐलुमिनियम ऑक्साइड, \(\mathrm{Al}_2\mathrm{O}_3\) का एक क्रिस्टलीय खनिज रूप है। अतः, \(\mathrm{D} \rightarrow (1)\)।

चरण 3: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
अतः, सही सुमेलन कूट \(\mathrm{A\ (3)\ B\ (4)\ C\ (2)\ D\ (1)}\) है।

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MATCHING_Q49 - Match furnaces and processes with metals and reactions

questiontext.text:
Match the items of Column I with items of Column II and assign the correct code:

Column IColumn II
(A) Blistered Cu(1) Aluminium
(B) Blast furnace(2) \(2\mathrm{Cu}_{2}\mathrm{O} + \mathrm{Cu}_{2}\mathrm{S} \longrightarrow 6\mathrm{Cu} + \mathrm{SO}_{2}\)
(C) Reverberatory furnace(3) Iron
(D) Hall-Heroult process(4) \(\mathrm{FeO} + \mathrm{SiO}_2 \longrightarrow \mathrm{FeSiO}_3\)
(5) \(2\mathrm{Cu}_{2}\mathrm{S} + 3\mathrm{O}_{2} \longrightarrow 2\mathrm{Cu}_{2}\mathrm{O} + 2\mathrm{SO}_{2}\)

स्तंभ I की मदों को स्तंभ II की मदों से सुमेलित कीजिए और सही कूट का चयन कीजिए:

स्तंभ Iस्तंभ II
(A) फफोलेदार Cu(1) ऐलुमिनियम
(B) वात्या भट्ठी(2) \(2\mathrm{Cu}_{2}\mathrm{O} + \mathrm{Cu}_{2}\mathrm{S} \longrightarrow 6\mathrm{Cu} + \mathrm{SO}_{2}\)
(C) परावर्तनी भट्ठी(3) आयरन
(D) हॉल-हेरॉल्ट प्रक्रम(4) \(\mathrm{FeO} + \mathrm{SiO}_2 \longrightarrow \mathrm{FeSiO}_3\)
(5) \(2\mathrm{Cu}_{2}\mathrm{S} + 3\mathrm{O}_{2} \longrightarrow 2\mathrm{Cu}_{2}\mathrm{O} + 2\mathrm{SO}_{2}\)

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Each metallurgical term or furnace in Column I corresponds to a specific metal or chemical reaction in Column II.

Step 2: Item-by-Item Matching
- Blistered \(\mathrm{Cu}\): Formed by the autoreduction reaction \(2\mathrm{Cu}_2\mathrm{O} + \mathrm{Cu}_2\mathrm{S} \longrightarrow 6\mathrm{Cu} + \mathrm{SO}_2\), where evolution of \(\mathrm{SO}_2\) gives a blistered appearance. Thus, \(\mathrm{A} \rightarrow (2)\).
- Blast furnace: Used for the extraction of iron from its oxide ores. Thus, \(\mathrm{B} \rightarrow (3)\).
- Reverberatory furnace: In copper extraction, iron oxide impurity is removed as slag in a reverberatory furnace via \(\mathrm{FeO} + \mathrm{SiO}_2 \longrightarrow \mathrm{FeSiO}_3\). Thus, \(\mathrm{C} \rightarrow (4)\).
- Hall-Heroult process: Used for the electrolytic extraction of aluminium. Thus, \(\mathrm{D} \rightarrow (1)\).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Therefore, the correct matching code is \(\mathrm{A\ (2)\ B\ (3)\ C\ (4)\ D\ (1)}\).

चरण 1: अवधारणात्मक सिद्धांत
स्तंभ I में प्रत्येक धातुकर्म पद या भट्ठी स्तंभ II में एक विशिष्ट धातु या रासायनिक अभिक्रिया से संबंधित है।

चरण 2: प्रत्येक मद का सुमेलन
- फफोलेदार \(\mathrm{Cu}\): स्वतः अपचयन अभिक्रिया \(2\mathrm{Cu}_2\mathrm{O} + \mathrm{Cu}_2\mathrm{S} \longrightarrow 6\mathrm{Cu} + \mathrm{SO}_2\) द्वारा बनता है, जहाँ \(\mathrm{SO}_2\) के निकलने से सतह फफोलेदार दिखाई देती है। अतः, \(\mathrm{A} \rightarrow (2)\)।
- वात्या भट्ठी: इसका उपयोग आयरन के ऑक्साइड अयस्कों से आयरन के निष्कर्षण के लिए किया जाता है। अतः, \(\mathrm{B} \rightarrow (3)\)।
- परावर्तनी भट्ठी: कॉपर निष्कर्षण में, आयरन ऑक्साइड की अशुद्धि को परावर्तनी भट्ठी में \(\mathrm{FeO} + \mathrm{SiO}_2 \longrightarrow \mathrm{FeSiO}_3\) के माध्यम से धातुमल के रूप में हटाया जाता है। अतः, \(\mathrm{C} \rightarrow (4)\)।
- हॉल-हेरॉल्ट प्रक्रम: इसका उपयोग ऐलुमिनियम के वैद्युत अपघटनी निष्कर्षण के लिए किया जाता है। अतः, \(\mathrm{D} \rightarrow (1)\)।

चरण 3: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
अतः, सही सुमेलन कूट \(\mathrm{A\ (2)\ B\ (3)\ C\ (4)\ D\ (1)}\) है।

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_AR_Q50 - Assertion Reason on Mond process for Nickel

questiontext.text:
In the following question a statement of assertion followed by a statement of reason is given. Choose the correct answer out of the given choices.

Assertion : Nickel can be purified by Mond process.

Reason : \(\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CO})_4\) is a volatile compound which decomposes at \(460\,\mathrm{K}\) to give pure \(\mathrm{Ni}\).

निम्नलिखित प्रश्न में एक अभिकथन के बाद एक कारण दिया गया है। दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर चुनिए।

अभिकथन : निकेल का शुद्धिकरण मॉन्ड प्रक्रम द्वारा किया जा सकता है।

कारण : \(\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CO})_4\) एक वाष्पशील यौगिक है जो \(460\,\mathrm{K}\) पर अपघटित होकर शुद्ध \(\mathrm{Ni}\) देता है।

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Assertion
Nickel is indeed purified by the Mond process (vapour phase refining), so the assertion is true.

Step 2: Evaluation of Reason and Causal Link
In the Mond process, impure nickel is heated in a stream of carbon monoxide at \(330\text{--}350\,\mathrm{K}\) to form volatile nickel tetracarbonyl, \(\mathrm{Ni(CO)}_4\). This volatile complex is then subjected to a higher temperature of about \(450\text{--}470\,\mathrm{K}\) (\(460\,\mathrm{K}\)) where it decomposes to give pure nickel metal and \(\mathrm{CO}\). Thus, the reason is true and correctly explains why nickel can be purified by the Mond process.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.

चरण 1: अभिकथन का मूल्यांकन
निकेल का शुद्धिकरण वास्तव में मॉन्ड प्रक्रम (वाष्प प्रावस्था परिष्करण) द्वारा किया जाता है, इसलिए अभिकथन सत्य है।

चरण 2: कारण और कार्य-कारण संबंध का मूल्यांकन
मॉन्ड प्रक्रम में, अशुद्ध निकेल को \(330\text{--}350\,\mathrm{K}\) पर कार्बन मोनोऑक्साइड की धारा में गर्म करके वाष्पशील निकेल टेट्राकार्बोनिल, \(\mathrm{Ni(CO)}_4\) बनाया जाता है। फिर इस वाष्पशील संकुल को लगभग \(450\text{--}470\,\mathrm{K}\) (\(460\,\mathrm{K}\)) के उच्च ताप पर गर्म करने पर यह अपघटित होकर शुद्ध निकेल धातु और \(\mathrm{CO}\) देता है। अतः, कारण सत्य है और यह सही ढंग से व्याख्या करता है कि मॉन्ड प्रक्रम द्वारा निकेल को क्यों शुद्ध किया जा सकता है।

चरण 3: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
अभिकथन और कारण दोनों सत्य हैं तथा कारण, अभिकथन की सही व्याख्या है।

answer.text: Both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
Both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
Assertion is true but reason is false.
Assertion is false but reason is true.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_AR_Q51 - Assertion Reason on Van Arkel method for Zirconium

questiontext.text:
In the following question a statement of assertion followed by a statement of reason is given. Choose the correct answer out of the given choices.

Assertion : Zirconium can be purified by Van Arkel method.

Reason : \(\mathrm{ZrI}_4\) is volatile and decomposes at \(1800\,\mathrm{K}\).

निम्नलिखित प्रश्न में एक अभिकथन के बाद एक कारण दिया गया है। दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर चुनिए।

अभिकथन : ज़िरकोनियम का शुद्धिकरण वान आरकेल विधि द्वारा किया जा सकता है।

कारण : \(\mathrm{ZrI}_4\) वाष्पशील है और \(1800\,\mathrm{K}\) पर अपघटित होता है।

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Assertion
Zirconium (\(\mathrm{Zr}\)) is purified by the van Arkel method to remove oxygen and nitrogen impurities, so the assertion is true.

Step 2: Evaluation of Reason and Causal Link
Crude zirconium is heated in an evacuated vessel with iodine at \(870\,\mathrm{K}\) to form volatile zirconium tetraiodide (\(\mathrm{ZrI}_4\)). The volatile \(\mathrm{ZrI}_4\) is decomposed over a tungsten filament electrically heated to about \(1800\,\mathrm{K}\), depositing pure zirconium. Therefore, the reason is true and correctly explains the assertion.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.

चरण 1: अभिकथन का मूल्यांकन
ऑक्सीजन और नाइट्रोजन की अशुद्धियों को दूर करने के लिए ज़िरकोनियम (\(\mathrm{Zr}\)) का शुद्धिकरण वान आरकेल विधि द्वारा किया जाता है, इसलिए अभिकथन सत्य है।

चरण 2: कारण और कार्य-कारण संबंध का मूल्यांकन
अशुद्ध ज़िरकोनियम को एक निर्वातित पात्र में आयोडीन के साथ \(870\,\mathrm{K}\) पर गर्म करके वाष्पशील ज़िरकोनियम टेट्राआयोडाइड (\(\mathrm{ZrI}_4\)) बनाया जाता है। वाष्पशील \(\mathrm{ZrI}_4\) को लगभग \(1800\,\mathrm{K}\) पर विद्युत द्वारा गर्म किए गए टंगस्टन तंतु पर अपघटित किया जाता है, जिससे शुद्ध ज़िरकोनियम निक्षेपित हो जाता है। अतः, कारण सत्य है और अभिकथन की सही व्याख्या करता है।

चरण 3: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
अभिकथन और कारण दोनों सत्य हैं तथा कारण, अभिकथन की सही व्याख्या है।

answer.text: Both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
Both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
Assertion is true but reason is false.
Assertion is false but reason is true.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_AR_Q52 - Assertion Reason on Froth Flotation and cresols

questiontext.text:
In the following question a statement of assertion followed by a statement of reason is given. Choose the correct answer out of the given choices.

Assertion : Sulphide ores are concentrated by Froth Flotation method.

Reason : Cresols stabilise the froth in Froth Flotation method.

निम्नलिखित प्रश्न में एक अभिकथन के बाद एक कारण दिया गया है। दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर चुनिए।

अभिकथन : सल्फाइड अयस्कों का सांद्रण फेन प्लवन विधि द्वारा किया जाता है।

कारण : फेन प्लवन विधि में क्रेसॉल फेन को स्थायी बनाते हैं।

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Assertion
Sulphide ores are concentrated by the froth flotation method, so the assertion is true.

Step 2: Evaluation of Reason and Causal Link
Cresols (and aniline) act as froth stabilisers in the froth flotation method, so the reason is also true. However, the reason why sulphide ores are concentrated by froth flotation is that sulphide ore particles are preferentially wetted by oil (collectors) while gangue particles are wetted by water—not because cresols stabilise the froth. Thus, the reason is not the correct explanation of the assertion.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.

चरण 1: अभिकथन का मूल्यांकन
सल्फाइड अयस्कों का सांद्रण फेन प्लवन विधि द्वारा किया जाता है, इसलिए अभिकथन सत्य है।

चरण 2: कारण और कार्य-कारण संबंध का मूल्यांकन
क्रेसॉल (और ऐनिलीन) फेन प्लवन विधि में फेन स्थायीकारक के रूप में कार्य करते हैं, इसलिए कारण भी सत्य है। तथापि, सल्फाइड अयस्कों को फेन प्लवन द्वारा सांद्रित करने का कारण यह है कि सल्फाइड अयस्क के कण तेल (संग्राहक) से अधिक आसानी से भीगते हैं जबकि आधात्री के कण जल से भीगते हैं—न कि इसलिए कि क्रेसॉल फेन को स्थायी बनाते हैं। अतः, कारण अभिकथन की सही व्याख्या नहीं है।

चरण 3: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
अभिकथन और कारण दोनों सत्य हैं परन्तु कारण, अभिकथन की सही व्याख्या नहीं है।

answer.text: Both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
Both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
Assertion is true but reason is false.
Assertion is false but reason is true.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_AR_Q53 - Assertion Reason on Zone refining for semiconductors

questiontext.text:
In the following question a statement of assertion followed by a statement of reason is given. Choose the correct answer out of the given choices.

Assertion : Zone refining method is very useful for producing semiconductors.

Reason : Semiconductors are of high purity.

निम्नलिखित प्रश्न में एक अभिकथन के बाद एक कारण दिया गया है। दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर चुनिए।

अभिकथन : अर्धचालकों के उत्पादन के लिए ज़ोन परिष्करण विधि बहुत उपयोगी है।

कारण : अर्धचालक उच्च शुद्धता के होते हैं।

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Assertion
Zone refining is extensively used to purify elements such as silicon, germanium, gallium, and indium used as semiconductors, so the assertion is true.

Step 2: Evaluation of Reason and Causal Link
Semiconductors require extremely high purity (ultrapure grade) for their electronic properties, so the reason is true. Because zone refining removes trace impurities down to parts per billion by exploiting their higher solubility in the molten zone, it is specifically useful for producing such high-purity semiconductors. Thus, the reason correctly explains the assertion.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.

चरण 1: अभिकथन का मूल्यांकन
अर्धचालकों के रूप में प्रयुक्त होने वाले सिलिकॉन, जर्मेनियम, गैलियम और इंडियम जैसे तत्वों के शुद्धिकरण के लिए ज़ोन परिष्करण का व्यापक रूप से उपयोग किया जाता है, इसलिए अभिकथन सत्य है।

चरण 2: कारण और कार्य-कारण संबंध का मूल्यांकन
अर्धचालकों को उनके इलेक्ट्रॉनिक गुणों के लिए अत्यधिक उच्च शुद्धता (अतिशुद्ध ग्रेड) की आवश्यकता होती है, इसलिए कारण सत्य है। चूँकि ज़ोन परिष्करण गलित ज़ोन में अशुद्धियों की उच्च विलेयता का उपयोग करके सूक्ष्म अशुद्धियों को भी हटा देता है, इसलिए यह ऐसे उच्च शुद्धता वाले अर्धचालकों के उत्पादन के लिए विशेष रूप से उपयोगी है। अतः, कारण अभिकथन की सही व्याख्या करता है।

चरण 3: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
अभिकथन और कारण दोनों सत्य हैं तथा कारण, अभिकथन की सही व्याख्या है।

answer.text: Both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
Both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
Assertion is true but reason is false.
Assertion is false but reason is true.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_AR_Q54 - Assertion Reason on hydrometallurgy and copper extraction

questiontext.text:
In the following question a statement of assertion followed by a statement of reason is given. Choose the correct answer out of the given choices.

Assertion : Hydrometallurgy involves dissolving the ore in a suitable reagent followed by precipitation by a more electropositive metal.

Reason : Copper is extracted by hydrometallurgy.

निम्नलिखित प्रश्न में एक अभिकथन के बाद एक कारण दिया गया है। दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर चुनिए।

अभिकथन : जलधातुकर्म में अयस्क को उपयुक्त अभिकर्मक में घोलना और उसके बाद अधिक विद्युत-धनात्मक धातु द्वारा अवक्षेपण शामिल है।

कारण : कॉपर का निष्कर्षण जलधातुकर्म द्वारा किया जाता है।

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Assertion
Hydrometallurgy indeed involves leaching (dissolving) the ore in a suitable aqueous reagent followed by precipitation (displacement) of the metal by a more electropositive metal (or \(\mathrm{H}_2\)), so the assertion is true.

Step 2: Evaluation of Reason and Causal Link
Low-grade copper ores are extracted by hydrometallurgy using acid or bacteria, followed by treatment with scrap iron or \(\mathrm{H}_2\), so the reason is true. However, the extraction of copper is merely an example of hydrometallurgy, not the explanation for what hydrometallurgy involves.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.

चरण 1: अभिकथन का मूल्यांकन
जलधातुकर्म में वास्तव में अयस्क को एक उपयुक्त जलीय अभिकर्मक में घोलना (निक्षालन) और उसके बाद अधिक विद्युत-धनात्मक धातु (या \(\mathrm{H}_2\)) द्वारा धातु का अवक्षेपण (विस्थापन) शामिल है, इसलिए अभिकथन सत्य है।

चरण 2: कारण और कार्य-कारण संबंध का मूल्यांकन
निम्न-कोटि के कॉपर अयस्कों से कॉपर का निष्कर्षण अम्ल या जीवाणुओं का उपयोग करके जलधातुकर्म द्वारा किया जाता है, जिसके बाद रद्दी लोहे या \(\mathrm{H}_2\) के साथ अभिक्रिया कराई जाती है, इसलिए कारण सत्य है। तथापि, कॉपर का निष्कर्षण केवल जलधातुकर्म का एक उदाहरण है, न कि इस बात की व्याख्या कि जलधातुकर्म में क्या शामिल है।

चरण 3: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
अभिकथन और कारण दोनों सत्य हैं परन्तु कारण, अभिकथन की सही व्याख्या नहीं है।

answer.text: Both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
Both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
Assertion is true but reason is false.
Assertion is false but reason is true.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQI_THEPBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q01 - Reaction of concentrated sulphuric acid with halides

questiontext.text: On addition of conc. \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{SO}_4\) to a chloride salt, colourless fumes are evolved but in case of iodide salt, violet fumes come out. This is because

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Concentrated sulphuric acid (\(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{SO}_4\)) acts both as a strong acid and as a moderately strong oxidising agent. The reducing power of hydrogen halides (\(\mathrm{HX}\)) increases down the group in the order \(\mathrm{HF} < \mathrm{HCl} < \mathrm{HBr} < \mathrm{HI}\).

Step 2: Evaluation
When conc. \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{SO}_4\) is added to a chloride salt, \(\mathrm{HCl}\) gas is evolved as colourless fumes. Because \(\mathrm{HCl}\) is a weak reducing agent, it is not oxidised by conc. \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{SO}_4\).

Step 3: Application
When conc. \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{SO}_4\) is added to an iodide salt, \(\mathrm{HI}\) is initially formed. However, \(\mathrm{HI}\) is a strong reducing agent and immediately reduces \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{SO}_4\) to \(\mathrm{SO}_2\), while \(\mathrm{HI}\) itself gets oxidised to \(\mathrm{I}_2\), which evolves as violet fumes:
\(2\mathrm{HI} + \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{SO}_4 \rightarrow \mathrm{I}_2 + \mathrm{SO}_2 + 2\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\)

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Violet fumes appear because \(\mathrm{HI}\) gets oxidised to \(\mathrm{I}_2\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQI_THEPBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q02 - Qualitative analysis of copper sulphide with ammonia

questiontext.text: In qualitative analysis when \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{S}\) is passed through an aqueous solution of salt acidified with dil. \(\mathrm{HCl}\), a black precipitate is obtained. On boiling the precipitate with dil. \(\mathrm{HNO}_3\), it forms a solution of blue colour. Addition of excess of aqueous solution of ammonia to this solution gives

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
In Group II qualitative analysis, passing \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{S}\) through an acidified solution precipitates \(\mathrm{Cu}^{2+}\) ions as black copper(II) sulphide (\(\mathrm{CuS}\)).

Step 2: Evaluation
On boiling the black \(\mathrm{CuS}\) precipitate with dilute \(\mathrm{HNO}_3\), it dissolves to form a blue aqueous solution of copper(II) nitrate, \(\mathrm{Cu(NO_3)_2}\):
\(3\mathrm{CuS} + 8\mathrm{HNO}_3 \rightarrow 3\mathrm{Cu(NO_3)_2} + 2\mathrm{NO} + 3\mathrm{S} + 4\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\)

Step 3: Application
When excess aqueous ammonia (\(\mathrm{NH}_3\)) is added to the blue solution containing \(\mathrm{Cu}^{2+}\) ions, a soluble, intensely coloured tetraamminecopper(II) complex ion is formed:
\(\mathrm{Cu}^{2+}(\mathrm{aq}) + 4\mathrm{NH}_3(\mathrm{aq}) \rightarrow \left[\mathrm{Cu(NH_3)_4}\right]^{2+}(\mathrm{aq})\)

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Addition of excess aqueous ammonia produces a deep blue solution of \(\left[\mathrm{Cu}\left(\mathrm{NH}_{3}\right)_{4}\right]^{2+}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQI_THEPBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q03 - Single and double bonds in cyclotrimetaphosphoric acid

questiontext.text: In a cyclotrimetaphosphoric acid molecule, how many single and double bonds are present?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
The molecule is cyclotrimetaphosphoric acid, which has the molecular formula \((\mathrm{HPO}_3)_3\) or \(\mathrm{H}_3\mathrm{P}_3\mathrm{O}_9\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Each phosphorus atom is pentavalent (forms 5 covalent bonds), oxygen is divalent, and hydrogen is monovalent.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Cyclotrimetaphosphoric acid has a six-membered cyclic ring consisting of three alternating phosphorus atoms and three oxygen atoms connected by \(\mathrm{P-O-P}\) linkages. Each phosphorus atom is also bonded to one oxo group (\(=\mathrm{O}\)) and one hydroxyl group (\(-\mathrm{OH}\)).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Count the double bonds:
Each of the 3 phosphorus atoms has one \(\mathrm{P=O}\) double bond, giving \(3\) double bonds.
Count the single bonds:
1. Ring \(\mathrm{P-O}\) single bonds: \(6\) single bonds (two per \(\mathrm{P}\) atom in the 6-membered ring).
2. Exocyclic \(\mathrm{P-O}\) single bonds to the \(-\mathrm{OH}\) groups: \(3\) single bonds (one per \(\mathrm{P}\) atom).
3. \(\mathrm{O-H}\) single bonds in the \(-\mathrm{OH}\) groups: \(3\) single bonds.
Total single bonds \(= 6 + 3 + 3 = 12\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Total valence bonds: \(3\) double bonds and \(12\) single bonds. Thus, cyclotrimetaphosphoric acid contains 3 double bonds and 12 single bonds.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQI_THEPBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q04 - Element capable of p-pi d-pi bonding

questiontext.text: Which of the following elements can be involved in \(\mathrm{p}\pi\text{–}\mathrm{d}\pi\) bonding?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
For an element to participate in \(\mathrm{p}\pi\text{–}\mathrm{d}\pi\) bonding, it must possess vacant \(d\)-orbitals of suitable energy in its valence shell.

Step 2: Evaluation
Boron (\(\mathrm{B}\)), carbon (\(\mathrm{C}\)), and nitrogen (\(\mathrm{N}\)) belong to the second period of the periodic table. Their valence shell is \(n = 2\), which contains only \(2s\) and \(2p\) orbitals and lacks \(d\)-orbitals.

Step 3: Application
Phosphorus (\(\mathrm{P}\)) belongs to the third period (\(n = 3\)), so it has vacant \(3d\) orbitals available in its valence shell. Therefore, phosphorus can form \(\mathrm{p}\pi\text{–}\mathrm{d}\pi\) bonds (for example, with oxygen in \(\mathrm{PO}_4^{3-}\) or \(\mathrm{P}_4\mathrm{O}_{10}\)).

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Phosphorus can be involved in \(\mathrm{p}\pi\text{–}\mathrm{d}\pi\) bonding.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQI_THEPBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q05 - Isoelectronic and isostructural ion pairs

questiontext.text: Which of the following pairs of ions are isoelectronic and isostructural?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
The ions to be compared are \(\mathrm{CO}_3^{2-}\), \(\mathrm{NO}_3^{-}\), \(\mathrm{ClO}_3^{-}\), and \(\mathrm{SO}_3^{2-}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Isoelectronic species have the same total number of electrons (or valence electrons). Isostructural species have the same hybridisation on the central atom and the same molecular geometry.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Total electrons \(=\) sum of atomic numbers of all atoms \(+\) negative charge. Geometry is determined by VSEPR theory via steric number \(=\frac{1}{2}(V + M - C + A)\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
For \(\mathrm{CO}_3^{2-}\):
Total electrons \(= 6 + 3(8) + 2 = 32\).
Central carbon atom has \(3\) bond pairs and \(0\) lone pairs (\(sp^2\) hybridised), giving a trigonal planar geometry.
For \(\mathrm{NO}_3^{-}\):
Total electrons \(= 7 + 3(8) + 1 = 32\).
Central nitrogen atom has \(3\) bond pairs and \(0\) lone pairs (\(sp^2\) hybridised), giving a trigonal planar geometry.

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Both \(\mathrm{CO}_3^{2-}\) and \(\mathrm{NO}_3^{-}\) have \(32\) electrons and trigonal planar structure, so they are isoelectronic and isostructural.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQI_THEPBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q06 - Bond dissociation enthalpy of halogen acids

questiontext.text: Affinity for hydrogen decreases in the group from fluorine to iodine. Which of the halogen acids should have highest bond dissociation enthalpy?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Bond dissociation enthalpy of a covalent \(\mathrm{H-X}\) bond depends inversely on the bond length and directly on the extent of orbital overlap between hydrogen and the halogen atom.

Step 2: Evaluation
Moving down Group 17 from fluorine to iodine, the atomic size of the halogen increases. Consequently, the \(\mathrm{H-X}\) bond length increases in the order \(\mathrm{H-F} < \mathrm{H-Cl} < \mathrm{H-Br} < \mathrm{H-I}\).

Step 3: Application
Since fluorine is the smallest halogen, the \(1s\text{–}2p\) orbital overlap in \(\mathrm{HF}\) is the strongest and the \(\mathrm{H-F}\) bond is the shortest, requiring the maximum energy to break.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
\(\mathrm{HF}\) has the highest bond dissociation enthalpy among the halogen acids.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQI_THEPBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q07 - Reducing strength of group 15 hydrides

questiontext.text:
Bond dissociation enthalpy of \(\mathrm{E\text{—}H}\) (\(\mathrm{E} = \text{element}\)) bonds is given below. Which of the compounds will act as strongest reducing agent?

Compound\(\mathrm{NH}_3\)\(\mathrm{PH}_3\)\(\mathrm{AsH}_3\)\(\mathrm{SbH}_3\)
\(\Delta_{\mathrm{diss}}(\mathrm{E\text{—}H})/\mathrm{kJ\,mol}^{-1}\)389322297255

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
The \(\mathrm{E\text{—}H}\) bond dissociation enthalpies are: \(\mathrm{NH}_3 = 389\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}\), \(\mathrm{PH}_3 = 322\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}\), \(\mathrm{AsH}_3 = 297\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}\), and \(\mathrm{SbH}_3 = 255\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
A hydride acts as a reducing agent by donating hydrogen atoms (or electrons) upon cleavage of the \(\mathrm{E\text{—}H}\) bond.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Reducing character of hydrides is inversely proportional to the \(\mathrm{E\text{—}H}\) bond dissociation enthalpy: the weaker the \(\mathrm{E\text{—}H}\) bond, the more readily hydrogen is released, and the stronger the reducing agent.

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Comparing the given values:
\(389 > 322 > 297 > 255\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}\).
\(\mathrm{SbH}_3\) has the lowest \(\mathrm{E\text{—}H}\) bond dissociation enthalpy (\(255\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}\)) because \(\mathrm{Sb}\) has the largest atomic size among the listed Group 15 elements, leading to the longest and weakest \(\mathrm{Sb\text{—}H}\) bond.

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Since \(\mathrm{SbH}_3\) loses hydrogen most easily, \(\mathrm{SbH}_3\) acts as the strongest reducing agent.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQI_THEPBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q08 - Properties of phosphine gas from white phosphorus

questiontext.text: On heating with concentrated \(\mathrm{NaOH}\) solution in an inert atmosphere of \(\mathrm{CO}_2\), white phosphorus gives a gas. Which of the following statement is incorrect about the gas?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
White phosphorus reacts with concentrated \(\mathrm{NaOH}\) solution in an inert atmosphere of \(\mathrm{CO}_2\) to produce phosphine gas (\(\mathrm{PH}_3\)):
\(\mathrm{P}_4 + 3\mathrm{NaOH} + 3\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O} \rightarrow \mathrm{PH}_3 + 3\mathrm{NaH}_2\mathrm{PO}_2\)

Step 2: Evaluation
Phosphine (\(\mathrm{PH}_3\)) is a colourless, highly poisonous gas with a rotten fish smell, and its aqueous solution decomposes in the presence of light to give red phosphorus and \(\mathrm{H}_2\).

Step 3: Application
Comparing basicity, phosphorus is larger and less electronegative than nitrogen, and the lone pair on phosphorus in \(\mathrm{PH}_3\) resides in a more diffused \(s\)-rich orbital compared to the \(sp^3\) orbital in \(\mathrm{NH}_3\). Therefore, \(\mathrm{PH}_3\) is a much weaker base than \(\mathrm{NH}_3\).

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The statement that the gas is more basic than \(\mathrm{NH}_3\) is incorrect.

answer.text: It is highly poisonous and has smell like rotten fish.
Its solution in water decomposes in the presence of light.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQI_THEPBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q09 - Tribasic acid forming three series of salts

questiontext.text: Which of the following acids forms three series of salts?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The number of series of salts formed by an acid corresponds to its basicity, which for oxoacids of phosphorus equals the number of ionisable \(\mathrm{P-OH}\) groups.

Step 2: Evaluation
- \(\mathrm{H}_3\mathrm{PO}_2\) has one \(-\mathrm{OH}\) group and two \(\mathrm{P-H}\) bonds, so it is monobasic (1 series of salts).
- \(\mathrm{H}_3\mathrm{BO}_3\) is a weak monobasic Lewis acid (accepts one \(\mathrm{OH}^-\) ion).
- \(\mathrm{H}_3\mathrm{PO}_3\) has two \(-\mathrm{OH}\) groups and one \(\mathrm{P-H}\) bond, so it is dibasic (2 series of salts).
- \(\mathrm{H}_3\mathrm{PO}_4\) (orthophosphoric acid) has three \(-\mathrm{OH}\) groups attached to phosphorus and is tribasic.

Step 3: Application
Because \(\mathrm{H}_3\mathrm{PO}_4\) has three ionisable protons, it forms three series of salts: \(\mathrm{NaH}_2\mathrm{PO}_4\), \(\mathrm{Na}_2\mathrm{HPO}_4\), and \(\mathrm{Na}_3\mathrm{PO}_4\).

Step 4: Final Conclusion
\(\mathrm{H}_3\mathrm{PO}_4\) forms three series of salts.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQI_THEPBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q10 - Cause of strong reducing behaviour of hypophosphorous acid

questiontext.text: Strong reducing behaviour of \(\mathrm{H}_3\mathrm{PO}_2\) is due to

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
In oxoacids of phosphorus, the reducing property is governed by the presence of \(\mathrm{P-H}\) bonds directly attached to the phosphorus atom.

Step 2: Evaluation
Hypophosphorous acid (\(\mathrm{H}_3\mathrm{PO}_2\), phosphinic acid) has a tetrahedral phosphorus centre bonded to one \(=\mathrm{O}\) atom, one \(-\mathrm{OH}\) group, and two \(\mathrm{H}\) atoms.

Step 3: Application
The two \(\mathrm{P-H}\) bonds can be readily oxidised to \(\mathrm{P-OH}\) bonds, making \(\mathrm{H}_3\mathrm{PO}_2\) a strong reducing agent (for example, reducing \(\mathrm{AgNO}_3\) to metallic \(\mathrm{Ag}\)).

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The strong reducing behaviour of \(\mathrm{H}_3\mathrm{PO}_2\) is due to the presence of one \(-\mathrm{OH}\) group and two \(\mathrm{P-H}\) bonds.

answer.text: Presence of two \(-\mathrm{OH}\) groups and one \(\mathrm{P-H}\) bond
Presence of one \(-\mathrm{OH}\) group and two \(\mathrm{P-H}\) bonds

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQI_THEPBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q11 - Thermal decomposition products of lead nitrate

questiontext.text: On heating lead nitrate forms oxides of nitrogen and lead. The oxides formed are

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Heavy metal nitrates decompose upon heating to give the metal oxide, brown nitrogen dioxide gas (\(\mathrm{NO}_2\)), and oxygen gas (\(\mathrm{O}_2\)).

Step 2: Evaluation
Lead(II) nitrate undergoes thermal decomposition according to the balanced equation:
\(2\mathrm{Pb(NO_3)_2(s)} \xrightarrow{\Delta} 2\mathrm{PbO(s)} + 4\mathrm{NO}_2\mathrm{(g)} + \mathrm{O}_2\mathrm{(g)}\)

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The oxides formed are \(\mathrm{NO}_2\) and \(\mathrm{PbO}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQI_THEPBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q12 - Allotropy in group 15 elements

questiontext.text: Which of the following elements does not show allotropy?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Allotropy in Group 15 elements depends on the ability of the element to form catenated or polymeric single-bonded structures.

Step 2: Evaluation
Phosphorus, arsenic, antimony, and bismuth exhibit allotropy. Nitrogen, however, has a very small atomic size, which leads to high interelectronic repulsion between non-bonding lone pairs on adjacent nitrogen atoms in a single \(\mathrm{N-N}\) bond.

Step 3: Application
Because the \(\mathrm{N-N}\) single bond is very weak compared to the \(\mathrm{N\equiv N}\) triple bond, nitrogen exists exclusively as discrete diatomic \(\mathrm{N}_2\) molecules and does not form polymeric allotropes.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Nitrogen does not show allotropy.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQI_THEPBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q13 - Maximum covalency of nitrogen

questiontext.text: Maximum covalency of nitrogen is

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The maximum covalency of an element is limited by the total number of orbitals available in its valence shell for bonding.

Step 2: Evaluation
Nitrogen has the ground-state valence electronic configuration \(2s^2 2p^3\). Its valence shell (\(n = 2\)) has only one \(2s\) orbital and three \(2p\) orbitals, and no \(2d\) orbitals exist.

Step 3: Application
With four valence orbitals in total, nitrogen can form a maximum of four covalent bonds (for example, in \(\mathrm{NH}_4^+\) or \(\mathrm{N}_2\mathrm{O}_5\)), which restricts its maximum covalency to 4.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The maximum covalency of nitrogen is 4.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQI_THEPBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q14 - Incorrect statement about nitrogen and phosphorus compounds

questiontext.text: Which of the following statements is wrong?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Bond strength of single homonuclear bonds in second-period elements with lone pairs is weakened by interelectronic repulsion between lone pairs on adjacent small atoms.

Step 2: Evaluation
- In a single \(\mathrm{N-N}\) bond, the small size of nitrogen atoms causes strong lone-pair–lone-pair repulsion, making the \(\mathrm{N-N}\) single bond weaker than the \(\mathrm{P-P}\) single bond.
- \(\mathrm{PH}_3\) has a lone pair of electrons on phosphorus and can act as a ligand with transition metals.
- \(\mathrm{NO}_2\) has an odd number of electrons (one unpaired electron), making it paramagnetic.
- In \(\mathrm{N}_2\mathrm{O}_5\), each nitrogen atom forms four covalent bonds (covalency is 4).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The statement that a single \(\mathrm{N-N}\) bond is stronger than a single \(\mathrm{P-P}\) bond is wrong.

answer.text: Single \(\mathrm{N-N}\) bond is stronger than the single \(\mathrm{P-P}\) bond.
\(\mathrm{PH}_3\) can act as a ligand in the formation of coordination compound with transition elements.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQI_THEPBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q15 - Brown ring test complex for nitrate ion

questiontext.text: A brown ring is formed in the ring test for \(\mathrm{NO}_3^-\) ion. It is due to the formation of

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
In the brown ring test for nitrate ions (\(\mathrm{NO}_3^-\)), freshly prepared \(\mathrm{FeSO}_4\) solution reduces \(\mathrm{NO}_3^-\) to nitric oxide (\(\mathrm{NO}\)) in the presence of concentrated \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{SO}_4\).

Step 2: Evaluation
The reactions involved are:
\(\mathrm{NO}_3^- + 3\mathrm{Fe}^{2+} + 4\mathrm{H}^+ \rightarrow \mathrm{NO} + 3\mathrm{Fe}^{3+} + 2\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\)
\(\left[\mathrm{Fe(H_2O)_6}\right]^{2+} + \mathrm{NO} \rightarrow \left[\mathrm{Fe(H_2O)_5(NO)}\right]^{2+} + \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\)

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The brown ring is due to the formation of the complex \(\left[\mathrm{Fe}\left(\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}\right)_{5}(\mathrm{NO})\right]^{2+}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQI_THEPBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q16 - Well characterised bismuth compound in +5 oxidation state

questiontext.text: Elements of group-15 form compounds in \(+5\) oxidation state. However, bismuth forms only one well characterised compound in \(+5\) oxidation state. The compound is

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Due to the inert pair effect, the stability of the \(+5\) oxidation state decreases down Group 15, while the \(+3\) oxidation state becomes progressively more stable. Thus, \(\mathrm{Bi(V)}\) is a very strong oxidising agent.

Step 2: Evaluation
Only the most electronegative and smallest halogen, fluorine, can stabilise bismuth in its \(+5\) oxidation state by forming \(\mathrm{BiF}_5\). Less electronegative elements like chlorine, oxygen, or sulphur are oxidised by \(\mathrm{Bi(V)}\) and cannot form stable, well-characterised \(\mathrm{Bi(V)}\) compounds.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The only well-characterised compound of bismuth in the \(+5\) oxidation state is \(\mathrm{BiF}_5\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQI_THEPBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q17 - Thermal decomposition of ammonium dichromate and barium azide

questiontext.text: On heating ammonium dichromate and barium azide separately we get

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Both ammonium dichromate and metal azides undergo thermal decomposition to liberate dinitrogen (\(\mathrm{N}_2\)) gas.

Step 2: Evaluation
1. Thermal decomposition of ammonium dichromate:
\((\mathrm{NH}_4)_2\mathrm{Cr}_2\mathrm{O}_7 \xrightarrow{\Delta} \mathrm{N}_2 + 4\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O} + \mathrm{Cr}_2\mathrm{O}_3\)
2. Thermal decomposition of barium azide (gives very pure \(\mathrm{N}_2\)):
\(\mathrm{Ba(N_3)_2} \xrightarrow{\Delta} \mathrm{Ba} + 3\mathrm{N}_2\)

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Heating ammonium dichromate and barium azide separately yields \(\mathrm{N}_2\) in both cases.

answer.text: \(\mathrm{N}_2\) with ammonium dichromate and \(\mathrm{NO}\) with barium azide
\(\mathrm{N}_2\mathrm{O}\) with ammonium dichromate and \(\mathrm{N}_2\) with barium azide
\(\mathrm{N}_2\mathrm{O}\) with ammonium dichromate and \(\mathrm{NO}_2\) with barium azide

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQI_THEPBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q18 - Stoichiometry of catalytic oxidation of ammonia

questiontext.text: In the preparation of \(\mathrm{HNO}_3\), we get \(\mathrm{NO}\) gas by catalytic oxidation of ammonia. The moles of \(\mathrm{NO}\) produced by the oxidation of two moles of \(\mathrm{NH}_3\) will be ______.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Moles of \(\mathrm{NH}_3\) oxidised \(= 2\text{ mol}\). Process: catalytic oxidation of ammonia in Ostwald's process for \(\mathrm{HNO}_3\) preparation.

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Oxygen is present in excess so that ammonia undergoes complete catalytic oxidation.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The balanced chemical equation for the catalytic oxidation of ammonia over a \(\mathrm{Pt/Rh}\) gauze catalyst at \(500\text{ K}\) and \(9\text{ bar}\) is:
\(4\mathrm{NH}_3\mathrm{(g)} + 5\mathrm{O}_2\mathrm{(g)} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{Pt/Rh},\,500\text{ K},\,9\text{ bar}} 4\mathrm{NO(g)} + 6\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O(g)}\)

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
From the stoichiometry of the balanced equation, \(4\text{ mol}\) of \(\mathrm{NH}_3\) produce \(4\text{ mol}\) of \(\mathrm{NO}\).
Therefore, the molar ratio \(\mathrm{NH}_3 : \mathrm{NO} = 1 : 1\).
For \(2\text{ mol}\) of \(\mathrm{NH}_3\):
\(\text{Moles of NO} = 2\text{ mol}\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Nitrogen atoms are conserved (\(2\text{ mol N}\) in \(\mathrm{NH}_3\) gives \(2\text{ mol N}\) in \(\mathrm{NO}\)). Thus, 2 moles of \(\mathrm{NO}\) are produced.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQI_THEPBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q19 - Oxidation state of phosphorus in sodium hypophosphite

questiontext.text: The oxidation state of central atom in the anion of compound \(\mathrm{NaH}_2\mathrm{PO}_2\) will be ______.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
The compound is \(\mathrm{NaH}_2\mathrm{PO}_2\). Its anion is \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{PO}_2^-\), with central atom phosphorus (\(\mathrm{P}\)).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Standard oxidation numbers: \(\mathrm{H} = +1\) and \(\mathrm{O} = -2\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The algebraic sum of oxidation numbers of all atoms in a polyatomic ion equals the net charge on the ion.

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Let the oxidation state of \(\mathrm{P}\) in \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{PO}_2^-\) be \(x\).
\(2(+1) + x + 2(-2) = -1\)
\(2 + x - 4 = -1\)
\(x - 2 = -1\)
\(x = +1\)

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking with the neutral salt \(\mathrm{NaH}_2\mathrm{PO}_2\): \(+1 + 2(+1) + (+1) + 2(-2) = 0\). Thus, the oxidation state of phosphorus is \(+1\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQI_THEPBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q20 - Identifying non-tetrahedral species

questiontext.text: Which of the following is not tetrahedral in shape?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Molecular shape is determined by the number of bond pairs and lone pairs around the central atom according to VSEPR theory.

Step 2: Evaluation
- \(\mathrm{NH}_4^+\): Central \(\mathrm{N}\) has \(4\) bond pairs and \(0\) lone pairs (\(sp^3\)) \(\rightarrow\) tetrahedral.
- \(\mathrm{SiCl}_4\): Central \(\mathrm{Si}\) has \(4\) bond pairs and \(0\) lone pairs (\(sp^3\)) \(\rightarrow\) tetrahedral.
- \(\mathrm{SO}_4^{2-}\): Central \(\mathrm{S}\) has \(4\) \(\sigma\)-bond pairs and \(0\) lone pairs (\(sp^3\)) \(\rightarrow\) tetrahedral.
- \(\mathrm{SF}_4\): Central \(\mathrm{S}\) has \(6\) valence electrons; \(4\) are used in forming \(\mathrm{S-F}\) bonds and \(2\) remain as \(1\) lone pair. This gives a steric number of \(5\) (\(sp^3d\) hybridisation, trigonal bipyramidal electron geometry).

Step 3: Application
With \(4\) bond pairs and \(1\) lone pair in an equatorial position, \(\mathrm{SF}_4\) adopts a see-saw shape rather than a tetrahedral shape.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
\(\mathrm{SF}_4\) is not tetrahedral in shape.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQI_THEPBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q21 - Identifying peroxoacids of sulphur

questiontext.text: Which of the following are peroxoacids of sulphur?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Peroxoacids of sulphur are oxoacids that contain at least one peroxo linkage (\(\mathrm{-O-O-}\)) in their structure.

Step 2: Evaluation
- \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{SO}_5\) (peroxomonosulphuric acid, Caro's acid) contains one \(\mathrm{-O-O-}\) linkage.
- \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{S}_2\mathrm{O}_8\) (peroxodisulphuric acid, Marshall's acid) contains one \(\mathrm{-O-O-}\) linkage between the two sulphur-centred tetrahedral units.
- \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{S}_2\mathrm{O}_7\) (pyrosulphuric acid or oleum) contains a \(\mathrm{S-O-S}\) oxide bridge, not a peroxo linkage.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
\(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{SO}_5\) and \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{S}_2\mathrm{O}_8\) are peroxoacids of sulphur.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQI_THEPBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q22 - Oxidation of carbon by hot concentrated sulphuric acid

questiontext.text: Hot conc. \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{SO}_4\) acts as moderately strong oxidising agent. It oxidises both metals and nonmetals. Which of the following element is oxidised by conc. \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{SO}_4\) into two gaseous products?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Hot concentrated \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{SO}_4\) oxidises metals and non-metals while itself being reduced to \(\mathrm{SO}_2\) gas.

Step 2: Evaluation
- Copper: \(\mathrm{Cu} + 2\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{SO}_4(\text{conc.}) \rightarrow \mathrm{CuSO}_4 + \mathrm{SO}_2\mathrm{(g)} + 2\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\) (only one gaseous product, \(\mathrm{SO}_2\)).
- Sulphur: \(\mathrm{S} + 2\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{SO}_4(\text{conc.}) \rightarrow 3\mathrm{SO}_2\mathrm{(g)} + 2\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\) (only one gaseous product, \(\mathrm{SO}_2\)).
- Zinc: \(\mathrm{Zn} + 2\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{SO}_4(\text{conc.}) \rightarrow \mathrm{ZnSO}_4 + \mathrm{SO}_2\mathrm{(g)} + 2\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\) (only one gaseous product, \(\mathrm{SO}_2\)).
- Carbon: \(\mathrm{C} + 2\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{SO}_4(\text{conc.}) \rightarrow \mathrm{CO}_2\mathrm{(g)} + 2\mathrm{SO}_2\mathrm{(g)} + 2\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\) (two gaseous products, \(\mathrm{CO}_2\) and \(\mathrm{SO}_2\)).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Carbon (\(\mathrm{C}\)) is oxidised by hot conc. \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{SO}_4\) into two gaseous products (\(\mathrm{CO}_2\) and \(\mathrm{SO}_2\)).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQI_THEPBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q23 - Oxidation state change of nitrogen in reaction with excess chlorine

questiontext.text: A black compound of manganese reacts with a halogen acid to give greenish yellow gas. When excess of this gas reacts with \(\mathrm{NH}_3\) an unstable trihalide is formed. In this process the oxidation state of nitrogen changes from

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Manganese dioxide (\(\mathrm{MnO}_2\), a black compound) oxidises concentrated hydrochloric acid (\(\mathrm{HCl}\)) to liberate greenish-yellow chlorine gas (\(\mathrm{Cl}_2\)):
\(\mathrm{MnO}_2 + 4\mathrm{HCl} \rightarrow \mathrm{MnCl}_2 + \mathrm{Cl}_2 + 2\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\)

Step 2: Evaluation
When excess \(\mathrm{Cl}_2\) reacts with \(\mathrm{NH}_3\), it forms the explosive, unstable nitrogen trichloride (\(\mathrm{NCl}_3\)):
\(\mathrm{NH}_3 + 3\mathrm{Cl}_2\text{ (excess)} \rightarrow \mathrm{NCl}_3 + 3\mathrm{HCl}\)

Step 3: Application
In \(\mathrm{NH}_3\), hydrogen has oxidation state \(+1\), so nitrogen has oxidation state \(-3\).
In \(\mathrm{NCl}_3\), chlorine is more electronegative than nitrogen and has oxidation state \(-1\), so nitrogen has oxidation state \(+3\).

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The oxidation state of nitrogen changes from \(-3\) to \(+3\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQI_THEPBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q24 - Reason for Bartlett using O2+PtF6- for xenon compounds

questiontext.text: In the preparation of compounds of \(\mathrm{Xe}\), Bartlett had taken \(\mathrm{O}_2^+\,\mathrm{PtF}_6^-\) as a base compound. This is because

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Neil Bartlett observed that \(\mathrm{PtF}_6\) oxidised molecular oxygen (\(\mathrm{O}_2\)) to form the ionic compound \(\mathrm{O}_2^+\mathrm{PtF}_6^-\).

Step 2: Evaluation
He noticed that the first ionisation enthalpy of molecular oxygen (\(1175\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}\)) is almost identical to the first ionisation enthalpy of xenon (\(1170\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}\)).

Step 3: Application
Reasoning that \(\mathrm{PtF}_6\) should similarly be able to oxidise xenon, Bartlett reacted \(\mathrm{Xe}\) with \(\mathrm{PtF}_6\) and prepared the first noble gas compound, \(\mathrm{Xe}^+\mathrm{PtF}_6^-\).

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Both \(\mathrm{O}_2\) and \(\mathrm{Xe}\) have almost the same ionisation enthalpy.

answer.text: both \(\mathrm{O}_2\) and \(\mathrm{Xe}\) have same electron gain enthalpy.
both \(\mathrm{O}_2\) and \(\mathrm{Xe}\) have almost same ionisation enthalpy.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQI_THEPBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q25 - Structure of phosphorus pentachloride in solid state

questiontext.text: In solid state \(\mathrm{PCl}_5\) is a

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
While \(\mathrm{PCl}_5\) exists as discrete trigonal bipyramidal molecules in the gaseous and liquid phases, it undergoes autoionisation in the solid state to achieve greater lattice stability.

Step 2: Evaluation
In the solid state, \(\mathrm{PCl}_5\) exists as an ionic solid composed of \(\left[\mathrm{PCl}_4\right]^+\) cations and \(\left[\mathrm{PCl}_6\right]^-\) anions.

Step 3: Application
- In \(\left[\mathrm{PCl}_4\right]^+\), phosphorus is \(sp^3\) hybridised with \(4\) bond pairs and \(0\) lone pairs, giving a tetrahedral geometry.
- In \(\left[\mathrm{PCl}_6\right]^-\), phosphorus is \(sp^3d^2\) hybridised with \(6\) bond pairs and \(0\) lone pairs, giving an octahedral geometry.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
In the solid state, \(\mathrm{PCl}_5\) is an ionic solid with \(\left[\mathrm{PCl}_4\right]^+\) tetrahedral and \(\left[\mathrm{PCl}_6\right]^-\) octahedral.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQI_THEPBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q26 - Decreasing order of oxidising power from reduction potentials

questiontext.text:
Reduction potentials of some ions are given below. Arrange them in decreasing order of oxidising power.

Ion\(\mathrm{ClO}_4^-\)\(\mathrm{IO}_4^-\)\(\mathrm{BrO}_4^-\)
Reduction potential \(E^\circ/\mathrm{V}\)\(E^\circ = 1.19\,\mathrm{V}\)\(E^\circ = 1.65\,\mathrm{V}\)\(E^\circ = 1.74\,\mathrm{V}\)

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Standard reduction potentials (\(E^\circ\)):
\(E^\circ(\mathrm{ClO}_4^-) = 1.19\text{ V}\)
\(E^\circ(\mathrm{IO}_4^-) = 1.65\text{ V}\)
\(E^\circ(\mathrm{BrO}_4^-) = 1.74\text{ V}\)

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Higher (more positive) standard reduction potential indicates a greater tendency for the species to gain electrons (be reduced).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Oxidising power is directly proportional to the standard reduction potential (\(E^\circ\)).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Arranging the \(E^\circ\) values in decreasing order:
\(1.74\text{ V} > 1.65\text{ V} > 1.19\text{ V}\).
Correspondingly, the decreasing order of oxidising power is:
\(\mathrm{BrO}_4^- > \mathrm{IO}_4^- > \mathrm{ClO}_4^-\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
\(\mathrm{BrO}_4^-\) has the highest reduction potential and \(\mathrm{ClO}_4^-\) the lowest, so the decreasing order of oxidising power is \(\mathrm{BrO}_4^- > \mathrm{IO}_4^- > \mathrm{ClO}_4^-\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQI_THEPBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q27 - Identifying isoelectronic halogen and interhalogen species

questiontext.text: Which of the following is isoelectronic pair?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Atomic numbers: \(\mathrm{C} = 6\), \(\mathrm{N} = 7\), \(\mathrm{O} = 8\), \(\mathrm{F} = 9\), \(\mathrm{Cl} = 17\), \(\mathrm{Br} = 35\), \(\mathrm{I} = 53\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Isoelectronic species have the same total number of electrons.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
\(\text{Total electrons} = \sum Z_i - \text{charge}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
- \(\mathrm{ICl}_2\) and \(\mathrm{ClO}_2\): \(53 + 2(17) = 87\) vs. \(17 + 2(8) = 33\) (not equal).
- \(\mathrm{BrO}_2^-\) and \(\mathrm{BrF}_2^+\):
\(\mathrm{BrO}_2^- = 35 + 2(8) + 1 = 52\) electrons.
\(\mathrm{BrF}_2^+ = 35 + 2(9) - 1 = 52\) electrons (equal).
- \(\mathrm{ClO}_2\) and \(\mathrm{BrF}\): \(17 + 2(8) = 33\) vs. \(35 + 9 = 44\) (not equal).
- \(\mathrm{CN}^-\) and \(\mathrm{O}_3\): \(6 + 7 + 1 = 14\) vs. \(3(8) = 24\) (not equal).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Both \(\mathrm{BrO}_2^-\) and \(\mathrm{BrF}_2^+\) have \(52\) electrons (and \(20\) valence electrons), so \(\mathrm{BrO}_2^-, \mathrm{BrF}_2^+\) is an isoelectronic pair.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQII_THEPBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q28 - Disproportionation of chlorine in hot sodium hydroxide

questiontext.text: If chlorine gas is passed through hot \(\mathrm{NaOH}\) solution, two changes are observed in the oxidation number of chlorine during the reaction. These are ______ and ______.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
When chlorine gas reacts with hot and concentrated \(\mathrm{NaOH}\) solution, it undergoes a disproportionation reaction, simultaneously getting reduced and oxidised.

Step 2: Evaluation
The balanced chemical equation is:
\(3\mathrm{Cl}_2 + 6\mathrm{NaOH}\text{ (hot, conc.)} \rightarrow 5\mathrm{NaCl} + \mathrm{NaClO}_3 + 3\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\)

Step 3: Application
- In \(\mathrm{Cl}_2\), the oxidation state of chlorine is \(0\).
- In \(\mathrm{NaCl}\), the oxidation state of chlorine is \(-1\) (reduction: \(0\) to \(-1\)).
- In \(\mathrm{NaClO}_3\), let the oxidation state of \(\mathrm{Cl}\) be \(x\): \(+1 + x + 3(-2) = 0 \Rightarrow x = +5\) (oxidation: \(0\) to \(+5\)).

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The two changes observed in the oxidation number of chlorine are \(0\) to \(+5\) and \(0\) to \(-1\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_PBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q29 - Properties and trends of halogens and halides

questiontext.text: Which of the following options are not in accordance with the property mentioned against them?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Periodic trends among halogens and their compounds depend on standard reduction potentials, polarising power and polarisability (Fajans' rules), bond dissociation enthalpies, and atomic size.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Relation
1. Oxidising power: Standard reduction potentials decrease from fluorine to iodine, so the oxidising power follows \(\mathrm{F}_2 > \mathrm{Cl}_2 > \mathrm{Br}_2 > \mathrm{I}_2\). This order is in accordance with the property.
2. Ionic character of metal halide: According to Fajans' rules, for a given metal cation \(\mathrm{M}^+\), a larger halide anion is more easily polarised, increasing covalent character and decreasing ionic character. Thus, ionic character follows \(\mathrm{MF} > \mathrm{MCl} > \mathrm{MBr} > \mathrm{MI}\). The stated order \(\mathrm{MI} > \mathrm{MBr} > \mathrm{MCl} > \mathrm{MF}\) is incorrect.
3. Bond dissociation enthalpy: Due to the very small size of fluorine atoms, strong inter-electronic repulsion between lone pairs weakens the \(\mathrm{F–F}\) bond compared to \(\mathrm{Cl–Cl}\) and \(\mathrm{Br–Br}\). The actual order is \(\mathrm{Cl}_2 > \mathrm{Br}_2 > \mathrm{F}_2 > \mathrm{I}_2\). Thus, \(\mathrm{F}_2 > \mathrm{Cl}_2 > \mathrm{Br}_2 > \mathrm{I}_2\) is incorrect.
4. Hydrogen–halogen bond strength: As halogen size increases from \(\mathrm{F}\) to \(\mathrm{I}\), the \(\mathrm{H–X}\) bond length increases and bond strength decreases, giving \(\mathrm{HI} < \mathrm{HBr} < \mathrm{HCl} < \mathrm{HF}\). This order is in accordance with the property.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The relations not in accordance with the stated properties are \(\mathrm{MI} > \mathrm{MBr} > \mathrm{MCl} > \mathrm{MF}\) for ionic character of metal halides and \(\mathrm{F}_2 > \mathrm{Cl}_2 > \mathrm{Br}_2 > \mathrm{I}_2\) for bond dissociation enthalpy.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_PBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q30 - Structure and bonding in white phosphorus

questiontext.text: Which of the following is correct for \(\mathrm{P}_4\) molecule of white phosphorus?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
White phosphorus consists of discrete tetrahedral \(\mathrm{P}_4\) molecules in which four phosphorus atoms occupy the four vertices of a regular tetrahedron.

Step 2: Evaluation of Bonding and Lone Pairs
Each phosphorus atom has five valence electrons (\(3s^2 3p^3\)). In the tetrahedral \(\mathrm{P}_4\) molecule, each phosphorus atom forms three single covalent \(\mathrm{P–P}\) bonds with the other three phosphorus atoms. Since a tetrahedron has 6 edges, there are six \(\mathrm{P–P}\) single bonds in total. Using three valence electrons in bonding leaves one lone pair of electrons on each of the four phosphorus atoms, giving a total of four lone pairs in the molecule.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The \(\mathrm{P}_4\) molecule of white phosphorus has six \(\mathrm{P–P}\) single bonds and four lone pairs of electrons.

answer.text: It has four lone pairs of electrons.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_PBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q31 - Properties of halogens and interhalogen compounds

questiontext.text: Which of the following statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Interhalogen compounds (\(\mathrm{XX}'_n\)) are formed by the combination of halogens of different sizes and electronegativities. Their reactivity and maximum coordination number depend on the radius ratio \(r_{\mathrm{X}}/r_{\mathrm{X}'}\) and bond strengths.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Statement
1. Radius ratio: Among stable halogens, iodine has the largest atomic radius and fluorine has the smallest atomic radius. Therefore, the radius ratio between iodine and fluorine is maximum.
2. Bond strength comparison: In general, the \(\mathrm{X–X}'\) covalent bond in interhalogen compounds is weaker than the \(\mathrm{X–X}\) bond in diatomic halogens (except the \(\mathrm{F–F}\) bond). Claiming that halogens (leaving \(\mathrm{F–F}\)) have a weaker \(\mathrm{X–X}\) bond than \(\mathrm{X–X}'\) is incorrect.
3. Maximum number of atoms: Because of the maximum radius ratio between iodine and fluorine, iodine forms \(\mathrm{IF}_7\), which has 8 atoms—the maximum number of atoms among all interhalogen compounds.
4. Reactivity: Due to the weaker \(\mathrm{X–X}'\) bond, interhalogen compounds are more reactive than halogens (except fluorine).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct statements are that the radius ratio between iodine and fluorine is maximum among halogens, the maximum number of atoms in interhalogen compounds is present in iodine fluoride (\(\mathrm{IF}_7\)), and interhalogen compounds are more reactive than halogen compounds.

answer.text: Among halogens, radius ratio between iodine and fluorine is maximum.
Leaving \(\mathrm{F—F}\) bond, all halogens have weaker \(\mathrm{X—X}\) bond than \(\mathrm{X—X}'\) bond in interhalogens.
Among interhalogen compounds maximum number of atoms are present in iodine fluoride.
Interhalogen compounds are more reactive than halogen compounds.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_PBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q32 - Properties and structure of sulphur dioxide

questiontext.text: Which of the following statements are correct for \(\mathrm{SO}_2\) gas?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Sulphur dioxide (\(\mathrm{SO}_2\)) is an acidic oxide of sulphur with \(sp^2\) hybridised central sulphur, possessing reducing and disinfecting properties.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Statement
